Traupman 364

minister, ministrī m.

noun, second declension

a minister of state

Classically an attendant, servant or helper, and an under-official (Lewis & Short); in Neo-Latin a minister of state (Morgan–Owens), as in Traupman’s minister prīmārius, prime minister. Rome had no ministers: public business was shared among magistrates elected for a year, and under the emperors among the emperor’s prefects and freedmen.

Other words

  • administer, administrī m. — a minister, a secretary of state

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 375–376; M-O s.v. minister, secretary, head of governmental ministry

    Classically an assistant or helper (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s word for the American secretaries of state, of the treasury and of the interior; Levi–Bini (p. 41) have rēgiī administrī, the king’s ministers.

  • minister pūblicus — a minister of state

    noun phrase: minister with the adjective pūblicus · also used · modern · M-O s.v. minister, cabinet member
